conversations.title: I was abused after meeting man on dating app
conversations.reply: That's horrific, and I'm so sorry you had to go through that. No one should ever feel unsafe or disrespected on a date.

conversations.title: Disability Gets Two Cents On The Philanthropic Dollar
conversations.reply: It's staggering how little attention is given to disability funding, and it's great to see people like this funder trying to make a change.

conversations.title: Friday briefing: How disabled creators are challenging an ableist world
conversations.reply: I love seeing disabled creators taking charge and challenging the status quo, it's about time we made accessibility a fundamental part of our culture.

conversations.title: Ways to recognize Disability Pride Month and practice inclusivity
conversations.reply: Disability Pride Month is a great opportunity to celebrate our identities and promote inclusivity, and it's fantastic to see people taking action to make their communities more accessible.

conversations.title: Campaign events should be accessible for all
conversations.reply: It's shocking that campaign events are still being held in inaccessible venues, excluding disabled people from the democratic process, and it's time we demanded better.

conversations.title: Business rates cut for pubs, clubs and live music venues to boost high streets
conversations.reply: Cutting business rates might help the nightlife industry, but let's not forget that accessible routes and venues are just as important as lower prices.

conversations.title: A Spectacular Arena is Set to Transform One of Britain’s Greatest Seaside Towns
conversations.reply: The new Phoenix Pavilion arena in Blackpool sounds exciting, but let's make sure it's accessible to everyone, including disabled people, from the start.

conversations.title: Sophie Morgan - TV Presenter & Disability Advocate
conversations.reply: Sophie Morgan is making a real impact with her advocacy work, using her platform to push for a more inclusive and accessible world. Her efforts are truly making a difference.

target_reply: Hey Sophie, love your work, you're making a real difference by challenging the ableist status quo and promoting inclusivity, let's chat about how we can work together to make the world a more accessible place.
funding: Nothing new today, but don't forget to check out UnLtd (unltd.org.uk) for funding opportunities, as well as Access to Work (gov.uk) and the Stelios Awards (around March)
moment: July is Disability Pride Month, and one honest way to join in is to have a brutally honest conversation with your friends and family about what accessibility really means ,  it's not just about ramps and elevators, it's about creating a culture that values disabled people's lives and contributions.
